claims.label: Context-dependent EfgA-associated formaldehyde resistance
claims.note: Native PA1-derived laboratory comparisons link loss of EfgA function to growth with externally supplied formaldehyde. This is not universal protection: EfgA was beneficial under endogenous formaldehyde stress. The study baseline CM2730 is already a laboratory derivative, not unmodified PA1. Reference-only UniProtKB:P0DX96 does not identify the tested alleles. Growth and translation responses are not MIC or clinical resistance categories; phenotypic heterogeneity remains distinct from this genotype association.
claims.phenotype_label: Source-reported relative formaldehyde resistance in laboratory growth assays

evidence.notes: DOI:10.1371/journal.pbio.3001208. Results, EfgB plays a secondary role in formaldehyde resistance; negative comparison in Figure 3 and conditional comparison in Figure 5. Supplement-only claims are not curated.
Species identity checked through UniProt taxonomy on 2026-10-14, release 2026_03. The PA1 reference lineage does not resolve the tested laboratory derivatives as a single strain or genome.

claims.label: Conditional EfgB-associated formaldehyde resistance
claims.note: The primary study supports a conditional EfgB contribution in EfgA-altered PA1-derived laboratory backgrounds; EfgB changes alone did not confer growth in the sole-formaldehyde-carbon comparison. The adenylate/guanylate cyclase annotation is putative, not demonstrated biochemical activity. Two dated UniProt queries returned no reference candidate; this is not evidence that the gene or protein is absent. No MIC, clinical category, exact allele, protein accession or experimental genome is assigned.
